subject: Retention carveout request and proposed purge timeline (Clearline Medical)
messages:
From: Pauline Hart <pauline.hart@clearlinemed.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: procure@clearlinemed.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Retention carveout request — Clearline Medical

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. We have an operational requirement for a temporary retention carveout while we run a migration and regulatory audit for a subset of patient records. Specifically, we need Redwood to hold backups and immutable snapshots for an additional 90 days for the following dataset: patient-messages and encounter-attachments for tenant clearline-prod (estimated 2.1TB).

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can apply a case-level snapshot hold (not full-tenant) for up to 90 days.
- The end-to-end deletion workflow and evidence you provide when snapshots are purged.
- Proposed purge timeline and any blackout/maintenance windows we should expect.

We attached a short request form with the dataset selector and business justification (Request_Form.pdf). Legal and procurement asked us to capture proposed timelines and a manifest format so we can sign an amendment if needed.

Appreciate an initial response today if possible — audit team is on a tight cadence.

Best,
Pauline Hart
Sr. PM, Security & Compliance
Clearline Medical

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Pauline Hart <pauline.hart@clearlinemed.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Retention carveout request — Clearline Medical

Pauline —

Thanks for the details and the form. We can support a scoped, temporary hold on snapshots for a named dataset and provide deletion evidence, but there are a few guardrails and a proposed operational cadence:

Proposed approach (high-level):
- Scoped snapshot hold: tag snapshots by case-id/tenant and mark them as "temporary-hold". These will be excluded from normal TTL-based prune jobs.
- Phased purge timeline: a staggered cutover to avoid spike IO — we suggest a two-phase approach (see attached proposed_cutover_schedule.xlsx):
  * Phase A (pre-clean): hold confirmation and manifest delivery — Target window: Nov 22–30, 2026
  * Phase B (controlled purge): staggered snapshot prune with audit manifests — Target window: Dec 15–22, 2026
- Evidence package: for each purge batch we can produce a manifest (CSV) with snapshot id, object keys, timestamps, and who requested the hold. We also provide a signed MD5 manifest and S3 object-level deletion logs for audit.
- Subprocessor access: limited engineering access only; we can provide an attestation of which subprocessors touched objects and an access log extract.

Open questions from our side:
1) Are you able to accept a staged retention of 75 days instead of 90? That reduces the operational window and aligns with our rolling purge cadence.
2) Do you require escrow of the snapshots (third-party escrow) prior to purge? That will affect timelines and cost.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll draft a narrow DPA amendment and an ops runbook (attachment) — CCing Kimberly (legal) and Marcus (ops).
- If Clearline agrees in principle to the staged dates above, Marcus will coordinate the purge windows with our SREs and provide the runbook.

I attached a proposed schedule spreadsheet that maps snapshot groups to purge phases (proposed_cutover_schedule.xlsx). Happy to jump on a 30-min call if the audit team prefers a quick sync.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, Pauline Hart <pauline.hart@clearlinemed.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retention carveout request — Clearline Medical

Mina / Pauline —

Quick legal note after reviewing Mina's proposal. We are open to a limited, case-level hold but need the following contractual guardrails before we proceed operationally:

Requested contract items / redlines (summary):
- Retention cap: Redwood requests limiting the temporary retention to a maximum of 75 days. If Clearline requires longer, we need explicit written approval from Redwood Legal and an agreed cost schedule.
- Audit evidence: Clearline must accept the deletion evidence format (manifest + S3 purge logs). We cannot produce escrow copies to a third party without a signed amendment.
- Subprocessor listing: Clearline requires an up-to-date list of subprocessors (with data-subset access levels) and an SSO audit for any vendor access during the hold window. We will attach our current subprocessor list and SOC 2 summary.
- DPA amendment: I’ve drafted a narrow amendment that adds a temporary retention carveout clause and a purge evidence schedule (DPA_amendment_draft_v1.docx). Please review and suggest edits.

Pauline — once you confirm that 75 days is acceptable we will finalize the amendment and schedule the purge windows with Ops. If you need a longer hold for regulatory reasons, flag the statutory basis so we can route for exec approval.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Pauline —

Thanks, Kimberly — useful redlines. Pauline, given legal's position, here's a compromise that should address the audit team's needs while keeping operational risk bounded:

Agreed compromise and final ops ask:
- Retention window: 75 days temporary hold (scoped by case-id).
- Phased purge cadence (detailed):
  * Controlled pre-clean (manifest population & tag verification): Nov 22–30, 2026
  * Hold extension cutover (final approval checkpoint): Dec 10, 2026
  * Staggered prune windows (per-shard batches): Dec 15–22, 2026
  * Final forensic sweep & confirmation (object-level purge logs generated): Jan 15, 2027
- Escrow: Instead of third-party escrow we will produce an encrypted SFTP manifest export and a signed MD5 manifest at each purge batch. If Clearline still requires escrow, we need a separate escrow contract and cost approval.
- Evidence deliverables: weekly manifests during the hold; batch manifests at each prune; final deletion package on Jan 15 (CSV + signed manifest + S3 purge logs). I attached an audit_manifest_template.csv and a short ops runbook (runbook-prune-ops.md) for review.

Operational notes / limitations:
- Subprocessor access: only engineers on the incident-ops group will have break-glass access; we will provide an access log extract for any access during the hold period.
- Cost impact: a scoped hold for 2.1TB will incur a temporary storage surcharge — Marcus will follow up with a cost estimate.

Next steps:
1) Pauline — confirm you accept the 75-day window and the phased timeline above.
2) If yes, Kimberly will finalize the DPA amendment and we’ll produce a signature-ready DocuSign link.
3) Marcus will coordinate SRE calendar blocks for the Dec prune windows and share a runbook rehearsal date.

If helpful, I can set a 20-minute sync tomorrow morning (Nov 20) to sign off.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: audit_manifest_template.csv, runbook-prune-ops.md
